transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-09-08 11:53 PT | Duration: 48m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Park (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (CTO, ApolloTech), Priya Shah (Head of ML), Carlos Mendes (Infra)
Shared: Deck: https://app.redwood.ai/decks/console-walkthrough, Cost spreadsheet: https://redwood.ai/sheets/apollo-cost-est

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um quick check, can hear me ok?
[00:12] Jordan Lee: yeah loud and clear, thanks Maya. we got Priya and Carlos on our side.
[00:18] Maya Chen: great. so goal for today is a quick console walkthrough \u0014 usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and then the cost breakdown that ties to your endpoints. we'll leave time for q&a and then next steps.
[00:33] Daniel Park: hey all. i'll do the demo side, show telemetry, how we map tokens to cost, and then go into batching/kv cache recommendations.
[00:45] Priya Shah: perfect, we mainly want to understand per-route variance \u0014 our chat vs summarization vs search rerank \u0014 and how that maps to cost. also curious about latency SLOs.
[00:58] Maya Chen: totally. Jordan, quick qualification \u0014 what's your expected volume? peaks and average? and are you leaning hosted or dedicated?
[01:12] Jordan Lee: expected steady-state 5 qps for chat, peaks to 50 qps during flash sales for short periods. embeddings for search rerank about 200 qps but small vectors. initially prefer hosted but might move to dedicated if costs ramp. timeline is Q4 eval for pilot.
[01:36] Carlos Mendes: also, security note \u0014 we need SOC2, SSO (SAML), and KMS integration; any residency constraints? we run mostly us-west and eu-west.
[01:48] Maya Chen: got it, we support SSO, KMS/HSM options and SOC 2 cert \u0014 we'll attach the security pack.
[01:56] Daniel Park: ok jump into the console \u0014 if you look at the overview, here's total token consumption across months, you can filter by route. (screen share)
[02:10] [02:10] Daniel Park: so this chart shows tokens/day, cost/day, and latency p95. see how cost spikes align to traffic spikes. note: transcription might say KV cash in places \u0014 it's KV cache.
[02:28] Priya Shah: can you filter by model family? we run a trimmed mix of open models and some fine-tuned variants.
[02:34] Daniel Park: yes \u0014 model catalog filter up here. we also tag routes so you can see chat-prod, summarizer, rerank.
[02:47] [02:47] Daniel Park: here's the per-route dashboard \u0014 left side is request volume and latency distribution; middle is token mix (prompt vs completion); right side is cost breakdown: compute vs model vs infra.
[03:05] Jordan Lee: that infra cost bucket, is that our own infra when using Redwood Private or Redwood Dedicated, or is it Redwood managed?
[03:14] Maya Chen: great question \u0014 for hosted API infra costs are in our managed bucket; for Dedicated or Private we'll show a cost allocation layer and you can plug in your own GPU cost numbers to get an apples-to-apples estimate.
[03:29] Carlos Mendes: how do you calculate per-route cost? is it purely tokens * model price or something fancier?
[03:36] Daniel Park: it's tokens * model unit + compute overhead + amortized cache and batching savings. for example if a route benefits from prefix/caching you'll see negative delta in the optimizer tab.
[03:49] [03:49] Priya Shah: show optimizer tab?
[03:52] Daniel Park: yep \u0014 optimizer suggests batching windows, a quantization profile (int8 or int4 depending on model), and KV cache candidate prefixes. here's an example where switching to int8 for rerank lowered cost 28% with negligible quality drop in our evals.
[04:12] Jordan Lee: what's the tradeoff on latency? our checkout chat needs sub-200ms p95.
[04:18] Daniel Park: with int8 we saw 5-12ms improvement for generation on Ampere/4th gen but quantization sometimes increases lat for long context models due to kernel mismatch \u0014 depends on seq length. optimizer flags routes where latency risk increases.
[04:36] [04:36] Carlos Mendes: can we set route-level SLOs and have auto-fallbacks? e.g., if a dedicated pool is saturated route falls back to hosted model variant?
[04:46] Maya Chen: yes \u0014 rollout policies support canary, A/B, and fallback to compatible variants by policy (latency or cost). we'll demo routing config briefly.
[04:58] Daniel Park: switching to the routing view \u0014 here you define policy: prefer dedicated pool, if p95 > 250ms then fallback to smaller model in hosted tier, or if error rate > 1% reroute.
[05:15] Priya Shah: ok, show a concrete example of per-route cost math for chat vs rerank.
[05:20] Daniel Park: sure \u0014 open cost breakdown spreadsheet (on screen). chat-prod: avg prompt 120 tokens, completion 40 tokens, model price x, so per request about $0.0012 before batching. rerank: prompt 20 tokens but 128 candidates = heavy compute; per request 0.006. optimizer flagged caching top-K context to lower average candidates scanned.
[05:46] Jordan Lee: those numbers \u0014 do they include prefix/KV cache savings?
[05:50] Daniel Park: the base numbers don't, optimizer section shows adjusted cost after cache/batching; example right here shows rerank down to 0.0029 with KV cache and batching.
[06:02] [06:02] Priya Shah: hmm curious about instrumentation \u0014 how do we get these metrics? do we push traces or do you ingest logs?
[06:10] Daniel Park: we ingest request-level telemetry via our SDK or you can ship logs/Prometheus. we map tokens, latency, model id, route tags. we'll share a sample exporter.
[06:22] Carlos Mendes: do you support open telem protocols?
[06:25] Daniel Park: yes \u0014 Prometheus metrics, OpenTelemetry traces, and S3/CloudWatch logs for payloads if you enable.
[06:33] [06:33] Maya Chen: quick aside \u0014 on compliance, we'll send SOC2 docs and your KMS integration guide after the call.
[06:40] Jordan Lee: good. also curious about historical analytics retention \u0014 we need 13 months for audit.
[06:47] Maya Chen: retention tiers are configurable; long term retention is an add-on. we'll include pricing for that.
[06:54] [06:54] Daniel Park: jumping back to console, here's a route-level heatmap \u0014 you can see time-of-day latency spikes, and overlay cost per token. useful for capacity planning.
[07:12] Priya Shah: can we set alerts on cost anomalies? we had a bad run with another vendor where cost spiked unexpectedly.
[07:18] Daniel Park: yes \u0014 anomaly detection and cost alerts with threshold + machine-learning baseline. can be routed to Slack, PagerDuty, or email.
[07:30] Jordan Lee: show the evals tie-in \u0014 how do you ensure optimizer recommendations don't degrade quality?
[07:37] Daniel Park: we attach prompt sets and A/B evals. optimizer recommendations are scored against eval suites; you can set tolerance e.g. max 1% drop in Rouge/ASR.
[07:50] [07:50] Carlos Mendes: any limitations for private deployment? we run air-gapped in a few regions.
[07:57] Maya Chen: our Private offering supports on-prem and VPC control plane with optional air-gap install. there are extra ops steps; we'll route you to the solutions engineer for a architecture session.
[08:08] Priya Shah: cool. about per-route attribution \u0014 how granular is it? can we break down by customer-id or by feature flag?
[08:16] Daniel Park: yes \u0014 we support custom tags and dimensions. you can slice by customer_id, feature_flag, model_version, etc.
[08:27] [08:27] Jordan Lee: ok something practical \u0014 we expect our chat to be very latency sensitive and rerank to be cost heavy. can you recommend immediate levers?
[08:36] Daniel Park: yes \u0014 for chat: prioritize low-latency kernels, enable KV cache for session prefixes, tune batching to small window size (20-50ms) to keep p95 under 200ms. for rerank: use quantized rerank model, reduce candidate set with cached hits and prefilter, or run rerank at lower frequency and cache results.
[08:58] Priya Shah: is there a way to simulate cost impact before applying changes?
[09:03] Daniel Park: yep \u0014 the optimizer sandbox allows you to run a hypothetical change against historical traffic and it will project cost and latency deltas.
[09:14] [09:14] Maya Chen: let's walk through an example sandbox run \u0014 i'll pick chat-prod and show results.
[09:20] Daniel Park: running now \u0014 baseline cost $X/day, after KV cache and int8 recommendation projected -32% cost, latency change +4ms p95. note: bucketed by hour so you can see peak impact.
[09:39] Jordan Lee: does the sandbox change anything live?
[09:42] Daniel Park: no \u0014 sandbox is simulation-only. any changes need to be promoted via the rollout UI which supports canaries.
[09:50] [09:50] Carlos Mendes: what about audit logs for changes and access? we need admin audit trails.
[09:56] Maya Chen: console has RBAC and admin audit logs that record config changes, who changed routing/policy, and timestamp. we'll include a sample audit export.
[10:06] Priya Shah: aside: in earlier conversations we heard Redwood has a cost-aware routing \u0014 can you show how to route by cost vs latency?
[10:14] Daniel Park: yes \u0014 policy engine supports weighting: you can set route preference = minimize cost subject to latency < 250ms. the engine runs a quick scoring function and picks compatible variant.
[10:26] [10:26] Jordan Lee: any mention of competitors? we compared Anthropic and OpenAI on some models; curious if Redwood can match latency.
[10:34] Daniel Park: depends on model/hardware \u0014 we publish verified perf profiles. in many cases we can match or beat cloud endpoints due to kernel-level optimizations and batched execution.
[10:47] Maya Chen: ok quick pause \u0014 do you want a deeper technical deep-dive after this or is this level good?
[10:54] Priya Shah: we want a technical deep-dive focused on perf and on-prem constraints. also a perf PoC where you run our traffic sample.
[11:02] Maya Chen: great. we'll set that up \u0014 Daniel will own PoC run.
[11:08] [11:08] Daniel Park: moving on \u0014 here's the per-route cost table (exportable CSV). notice we have a column for \"optimizer potential\" which is percent cost reducible. you can click into each route to see suggested changes and expected eval delta.
[11:25] Carlos Mendes: can we integrate this with our billing system? we need to correlate cost to internal chargebacks.
[11:31] Daniel Park: yes \u0014 you can export allocation reports by team/route and push to S3 or BigQuery; we also have an API to pull cost reports.
[11:40] [11:40] Priya Shah: show error/failure breakdown. our last vendor had high 5xx for large contexts.
[11:46] Daniel Park: here's a failures view \u0014 error rate by model id and cause (OOM, timeouts, infra). you can set alerts and auto-disable heavy routes.
[11:56] Jordan Lee: curious \u0014 what's the process to move to Dedicated later? do we have to re-architect?
[12:02] Maya Chen: no big re-architecture \u0014 we support consistent API and config. Dedicated is about capacity reservation and private pools; there's a migration plan and canary steps handled by our SRE team.
[12:14] [12:14] Priya Shah: ok show how to schedule a canary.
[12:18] Daniel Park: here in rollout tab create variation, target 5% of traffic, monitor key metrics for 2 hours, then ramp. you can set auto-rollback thresholds.
[12:30] Maya Chen: i'm going to surface some docs in chat \u0014 security pack, pricing examples, and a PoC checklist.
[12:37] [12:37] Jordan Lee: thanks. can you call out what you need from us for the PoC?
[12:42] Daniel Park: traffic sample (1 week), schema for requests, key routes to evaluate, and any eval prompt sets. metadata mapping for customer_id and route tags.
[12:52] Priya Shah: we'll share that by next Friday.
[12:55] [12:55] Maya Chen: perfect \u0014 next steps: send pricing, schedule PoC, and attach SOC2 docs.
[13:02] Jordan Lee: one more question on quantization \u0014 how do you validate quality? we have sensitive content so hallucination rates matter.
[13:09] Daniel Park: we run eval suites with A/B tests; optimizer uses your prompts to validate quality and optionally run a human-in-the-loop check before promoting changes.
[13:20] [13:20] Carlos Mendes: latency \u0014 do you provide p99 or p95 telemetry? we need p99 for infra sizing.
[13:26] Daniel Park: both \u0014 console shows p50/p95/p99 and histograms.
[13:31] Maya Chen: ok we're about midway. any other big blockers?
[13:35] Priya Shah: nothing else; main risks are cost unpredictability and ensuring latency SLOs.
[13:41] Maya Chen: understood. we'll focus PoC on those.
[13:45] [13:45] Daniel Park: now a quick look at alerts and runbook integration \u0014 you can attach a runbook to an alert with steps to failover to hosted variant.
[13:57] Jordan Lee: nice. can you email the runbook samples?
[14:00] Maya Chen: yes \u0014 will include sample runbooks.
[14:04] [14:04] Priya Shah: what about cost forecasting for seasonal spikes?
[14:09] Daniel Park: forecasting uses historical seasonality + capacity model; you can set reserved capacity to cap spend and enable burst policy.
[14:21] Jordan Lee: show reserved capacity UI?
[14:24] Daniel Park: here \u0014 commit level, expected throughput, and overage policy. helpful if you want predictable spend during holiday sales.
[14:36] [14:36] Carlos Mendes: we will likely start hosted for eval, then commit to Dedicated if numbers make sense.
[14:43] Maya Chen: that path is common. we'll provide a cost comparison for hosted vs dedicated with your numbers.
[14:51] [14:51] Daniel Park: quick Q from my side \u0014 what SLA do you need for pilot?
[14:55] Jordan Lee: we need p95 < 200ms for chat and 99.9% uptime during business hours.
[15:03] Maya Chen: noted \u0014 we'll include latency SLO targets and proposed committed capacity.
[15:08] [15:08] Priya Shah: any final notes on per-route dashboards? can we embed them in our internal tools?
[15:15] Daniel Park: yes \u0014 dashboards are embeddable via secure links and we have an API to pull route metrics programmatically.
[15:24] Jordan Lee: great, thanks.
[15:26] [15:26] Maya Chen: recap quick: Maya send pricing + security pack; Daniel run perf PoC and share exporter; Apollo to send traffic sample and eval prompts. schedule PoC week of Sept 21.
[15:40] Priya Shah: we'll target that.
[15:43] [15:43] Carlos Mendes: thanks everyone.
[15:45] Maya Chen: thank you \u0014 we'll follow up with docs and calendar invites.
[15:51] Jordan Lee: bye.
[48:00] Recording ends

Notes: transcript has small transcription artifacts (e.g., \"KV cash\" instead of KV cache, \"Redwood Dedicate\"), occasional speaker mislabels in the auto-gen \u0014 cleaned minimally above.
